Production Order — Edit

The Production Order form enables you to manage the manufacturing process by documenting the conversion of raw materials and components into finished products.

Production orders serve as authorization to begin production and help plan material requirements while tracking the entire manufacturing process.

Why Use Production Orders

Production orders are essential for manufacturing businesses, providing a systematic way to track material consumption, labor costs, and overhead allocation during the production process.

They ensure accurate inventory valuation by capturing all costs associated with creating finished goods, including direct materials, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead.

Creating a Production Order

When creating a production order, specify the finished goods to be produced and their quantities.

List all raw materials and components required, including quantities needed for the production run.

Add any non-inventory costs such as labor, utilities, or other manufacturing expenses.

Tracking and Completion

You can track the order through various stages of completion and record actual versus planned consumption.

The system automatically adjusts inventory levels when the order is completed, decreasing raw materials and increasing finished goods.

This form contains the following fields:

Date

Enter the date of production. This determines when inventory movements and costs are recorded.

Raw materials are consumed and finished goods are created on this date, affecting inventory valuations.

Reference

Enter a reference number for this production order. This could be a batch number or production run identifier.

References help track production batches for quality control, recalls, and cost analysis purposes.

Inventory Location

Select the inventory location where the finished goods will be stored after production.

Raw materials are consumed from this same location unless you use inventory transfers first.

Description

Optionally, add a description for this production order, such as product specifications or production notes.

Descriptions help document special production requirements, quality standards, or customer specifications.

Finished item

Select the finished inventory item being produced. This is the output of the production process.

The system will increase the quantity on hand of this item and calculate its cost based on inputs.

Qty

Enter the quantity of finished goods produced. The unit depends on the selected inventory item.

This quantity will be added to inventory at a cost calculated from the consumed materials and expenses.

Bill of materials

Enter the raw materials and components consumed in production. Each line represents an ingredient or component.

The cost of these materials will be transferred from raw material inventory to finished goods inventory.

Add non-inventory cost into production

Check this box to include non-inventory costs (like labor or overhead) in the production cost calculation.

This allows you to capitalize direct labor and manufacturing overhead into the cost of finished goods.

ExpenseItems

If including non-inventory costs, enter the expense accounts and amounts to add to production cost.

These costs are removed from expenses and added to the inventory value of the finished goods produced.
